description_summary: 12-month unduplicated enrollment headcounts by undergraduate or graduate level, sex, and race/ethnicity. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and EFFYLEV and includes total men and women counts plus counts for the race/ethnicity categories; because 2007-08 was the first year of a three-year transition, the table contains old, new, and derived race/ethnicity variables, including the new Two or more race category. Reporting was optional in even-numbered years, so 2008 (even) may have missing institution-level data.

12-month instructional activity measured in undergraduate and graduate credit hours and/or contact hours, used to derive 12-month full-time-equivalent enrollment. Each record represents an institution-level activity record by instructional level, identified by UNITID and the applicable undergraduate/graduate level variable. Reporting was optional in even-numbered years, so 2008 (even) may have missing institution-level data.

Institution-level academic library data for 2007-08, including library characteristics, collections, expenditures, and services. This is a subset of variables retained for comparability with the Academic Libraries collection introduced into IPEDS in 2014-15; it applies only to degree-granting institutions, and expenditure fields are available only for institutions with total expenditures over $100,000. No separate even- or odd-year reporting restriction is stated.

Awards conferred from July 1, 2007, through June 30, 2008, broken down by 6-digit CIP program, first or second major, award level, race/ethnicity, and gender. The table has multiple records per institution, uniquely identified by UNITID, CIPCODE, MAJORNUM, and AWLEVEL; each record includes total awards and counts by gender and race/ethnicity. Because 2007-08 was the first year of a three-year transition, it contains both old and new race/ethnicity variables, plus derived combined categories and the new Two or more race category.

Fall enrollment counts broken down by gender, full- or part-time attendance status, and student level. Each record is uniquely identified by IPEDS ID (UNITID) and attendance status/student level (EFLEVEL).

Fall enrollment counts broken down by race/ethnicity, gender, full- or part-time attendance status, and student level. Each record is uniquely identified by IPEDS ID (UNITID) and attendance status/student level (EFALEVEL); Fall 2008 is the first year of the two-year transition to new race/ethnicity categories, so the table includes old, new, and derived race/ethnicity variables.

Fall enrollment counts broken down by age category, gender, full- or part-time attendance status, and student level. Each record is uniquely identified by IPEDS ID (UNITID), age category (EFBAGE), and student level (LSTUDY). Enrollments by age are optional in even-numbered years, so 2008 (even) has data where institutions reported it.

First-time freshman counts broken down by state of residence, including the number who graduated from high school the previous year. Each record is uniquely identified by IPEDS ID (UNITID) and state of residence (EFCSTATE); residence reporting is optional in odd-numbered years, so 2008 (even) is not an optional year and has data.

Enrollment counts for selected major fields of study—Education, Engineering, Biological Sciences/Life Sciences, Mathematics, Physical Sciences, Business, Law, Dentistry, and Medicine—broken down by race/ethnicity, gender, full- or part-time attendance status, and student level. The table covers 4-year institutions only, and each record is uniquely identified by IPEDS ID (UNITID), major field of study, attendance status, and student level (EFCIPLEV); Fall 2008 includes old, new, and derived race/ethnicity variables during the two-year category transition.

Institution-level measures of total entering class size, first-year retention rate, and student-to-faculty ratio, restricted to institutions with undergraduate students. Entering-class data are collected only from academic-year institutions, and short programs of less than one year do not have retention data.

Institution-level student-to-faculty ratio for institutions with undergraduate students. This is the first collection year (2008-09); beginning in 2009-10, the ratio moved to the EFnnnnD table with entering-class and retention data.

Institutional revenues, expenditures, assets, and liabilities for public institutions using GASB accounting standards. Each record is an institution, and fiscal year 2008 is a transition year in which the institution may have used either the new aligned GASB form or the older unaligned form; the F_VER response flag identifies the form used. The aligned form adds natural-category reporting for operations and maintenance and changes how depreciation is reported.

Institutional revenues, expenditures, assets, and liabilities for private not-for-profit institutions and public institutions using FASB accounting standards. Each record is an institution; the aligned FASB form can distinguish unrestricted, temporarily restricted, and permanently restricted revenue by source, while 2008 also includes institutions using the older unaligned form. The F_VER response flag identifies the finance form used.

Institutional revenues, expenditures, assets, and liabilities for private for-profit institutions using FASB accounting standards. Each record is an institution, with expenditures reported by category rather than the GASB/FASB institutional functional-and-natural expense structure used in the other finance tables.

Graduation-rate cohort counts for four-year and two-year institutions, broken down by gender and race/ethnicity, including enrollment, completion, bachelor’s completion at 100%, 125%, and 150% of normal time, and transfer-out outcomes. Records are uniquely defined by IPEDS ID (UNITID) and cohort/graduation-status code (GRTYPE); four-year records distinguish bachelor’s degree-seeking students from students seeking other degrees or certificates, while two-year records use the 2005 full-time, first-time cohort. Because 2008 began the three-year race/ethnicity reporting transition, the table includes old, new, and derived combined race/ethnicity variables, including Two or more races.

Graduation-rate counts for the 2005 cohort at less-than-two-year institutions, including students enrolled, those completing a degree or certificate within 150% of normal time, and those transferring out. The grain is institution (IPEDS ID/UNITID), restricted to full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates at less-than-two-year institutions.

Graduation and completion counts for full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates, reported in the one-time Spring 2008 supplemental collection for student status as of August 31, 2008. The table is organized by institution and sector/level—4-year versus less-than-4-year—and by cohort year: 2000 for 4-year bachelor’s-degree-seeking students and 2004 for less-than-4-year students. It reports the number enrolled and the number completing within 100%, 150%, or 200% of normal time; 4-year completions must be bachelor’s degrees, while less-than-4-year completions may be any degree or certificate.

Fall staff counts broken down by full- or part-time status, medical-school status, occupational category, and tenure status. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and EAPRECTP, which combines occupational category, tenure status, and full- or part-time status.

Payroll staff counts broken down by occupational category, full- or part-time status, race/ethnicity, and gender, using old, new, and derived race/ethnicity variables during the 2008 transition. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and SABDTYPE; race/ethnicity and gender reporting was optional in even-numbered years, so 2008 (even) has incomplete data for many institutions.

Employee payroll counts broken down by primary function or occupation, race/ethnicity, and gender, using old, new, and derived race/ethnicity variables during the 2008 transition. The table applies to degree-granting institutions with fewer than 15 full-time employees, all nondegree-granting institutions, and related administrative offices; each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and SCNLEVEL. Race/ethnicity and gender reporting was optional in even-numbered years, so 2008 (even) has incomplete data for many institutions.

Full-time instruction/research/public-service staff counts broken down by faculty and tenure status, academic rank, race/ethnicity, and gender, using old, new, and derived race/ethnicity variables during the 2008 transition. The table applies to degree-granting institutions with at least 15 full-time employees and related administrative offices; each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and ARANK, which combines faculty status and academic rank. Race/ethnicity and gender reporting was optional in even-numbered years, so 2008 (even) has incomplete data for many institutions.

Full-time new-hire counts broken down by primary occupation, race/ethnicity, and gender, using old, new, and derived race/ethnicity variables during the 2008 transition. The table applies to degree-granting institutions with at least 15 full-time employees and related administrative offices; each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and SGTYPE, the primary-occupation category. Race/ethnicity and gender reporting was optional in even-numbered years, so 2008 (even) has incomplete data for many institutions.

Counts and salary outlays for full-time nonmedical instructional staff broken down by gender, academic rank, and contract length, including 9/10-month, 11/12-month, and equated 9/10-month contracts. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID, ARANK, and CONTRACT.
Counts of full-time nonmedical instructional faculty with contracts shorter than nine months, broken down by gender and academic rank. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and ARANK.

Fringe-benefit participation, total expenditures, and average expenditures for full-time nonmedical instructional staff broken down by contract length and benefit-plan type. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and BENTYPE.

Full-time nonmedical instructional staff counts broken down by faculty status, contract length, gender, and academic rank; this table is restricted to 4-year institutions. Each record is identified by UNITID, CONTRACT, and ARANK.

Response-status records by institution and survey component, identifying response, imputation, applicability, parent/child or multi-campus reporting, and revised submissions in final or revised releases. The row grain is institution by survey component.

Institution directory records for each institution, including identifying and contact information, website links, active and Title IV status, and institution-level control, level, highest award, and Carnegie classification variables. The row grain is one institution.

Institution-level records on educational offerings, award levels, organization and control, affiliations, special learning opportunities, services, and athletic associations, plus applicants, admissions, and test scores. Admissions and test-score fields apply only to institutions that do not have an open-admission policy; the row grain is one institution.

Full-academic-year student charges for institutions with predominantly credit-hour academic programs using a semester, quarter, trimester, 4-1-4, or other academic calendar. Institution-level fields cover full-time undergraduate and graduate tuition and required fees, part-time per-credit charges, first-professional charges, and published full-time first-time undergraduate price of attendance; the row grain is one institution.

Student charges by vocational or occupational program for institutions using clock hours or primarily occupational credit-hour programs, reported for the full program length. Records include the number of programs, price of attendance for the largest program, and tuition, fees, and books and supplies for up to five additional programs; the row grain is institution by program.
Institution-level mission statement records containing either the institution's mission statement or a web address for it. The row grain is one institution.

Percentage of an institution’s Fall 2008 undergraduate students who are formally registered with the institution’s disability services office or equivalent. The one-time spring 2008-09 supplemental collection covers all undergraduates enrolled in Fall 2008; the measure is institution-level, with the percentage of all undergraduates as the reported value. Disabilities data moved into the regular Institutional Characteristics survey beginning in 2009-10.

Student financial aid counts and average aid amounts by source and type for full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students at each institution. It covers aid received from July 1, 2007, through June 30, 2008; reporting is optional in even-numbered years, so 2008 (even) may have institutions without submitted data. Each record is identified by institution, with measures for federal grants (including Pell and other federal grants), state or local grants, institutional grants, federal student loans, nonfederal student loans, and total grant dollars; Pell recipient counts and total undergraduate grant dollars are available for this year.
